# Requisitos de solver, geração e dificuldade: Checklist

**Purpose**: Revisão padrão da qualidade dos requisitos de resolução, geração Killer Sudoku, dificuldade, limites e cancelamento antes da implementação.
**Created**: 2026-10-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Audience/Timing**: Author self-review before implementation.
**Focus/Depth**: Whole feature; standard review of completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and scenario coverage.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the Sudoku/Killer structural constraints for generated puzzles listed or explicitly delegated to the authoritative rules in feature 001? [Completeness, Dependency, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK002 Are the exact technique sets for Easy, Medium, Hard, and Expert included in the normative feature requirements, including at least one Expert-capable technique? [Gap, Spec §FR-005–007, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK003 Does the requirements contract define what “necessary techniques” means when multiple logical steps or solution paths are available? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK004 Are the expected outcome and caller-visible meaning of an unclassifiable puzzle specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK005 Are the source, units, and exhaustion behavior of attempt/time budgets specified, with production defaults tied to the promised target-device measurements? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK006 Are generated puzzle givens defined, including whether the standard generated Killer puzzle starts with any filled cells? [Gap, Spec §Key Entities, §US2]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is “inconsistent puzzle” distinguished clearly from a structurally invalid definition and from a valid definition with no solution? [Ambiguity, Spec §US1, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK008 Does the solution-count requirement make clear whether reporting “two or more” is sufficient, rather than requiring an exact count of every solution? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §SC-002]
- [x] CHK009 Does “explicit unavailability” define the information the caller receives, such as exhaustion reason and attempt count, without exposing a partial puzzle? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §SC-005]
- [x] CHK010 Is reproducibility scoped to the same seed, requested difficulty, options, catalog/algorithm version, and supported runtime? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 Is cancellation clearly distinct from budget exhaustion and ordinary no-solution/unavailable outcomes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, §FR-010]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK012 Are the statements that projects/solution do not exist and that toolchain gates cannot run reconciled with the current repository state documented in the plan? [Conflict, Spec §§2, 4; Plan §Structure Decision]
- [x] CHK013 Are the difficulty technique names and definitions consistent across this feature, the PRD, the plan, and feature 003’s hint scope? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006; Plan §Research]
- [x] CHK014 Do the requirements keep computational solving, logical classification, and player-facing explanations as distinct responsibilities? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §Contracts & Limites]
- [x] CHK015 Is the no-fallback rule consistent in the user story, edge cases, FR-010, and SC-005, including which requested difficulty is retained? [Consistency, Spec §US2, §Edge Cases, §FR-010, §SC-005]

## Requirement Measurability

- [x] CHK016 Can a reviewer objectively determine which documented profile classifies a puzzle, including tier boundaries and the catalog version used? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK017 Is cancellation responsiveness measurable enough to support “sem bloquear a navegação,” in addition to the no-partial-publication outcome? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008, §SC-004]
- [x] CHK018 Are the target devices, benchmark measures, and decision point for setting production attempt/time limits defined before the generator is released? [Measurability, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-010, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK019 Can reproducibility be objectively assessed from a defined set of equal inputs and expected-equal generation outputs? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §Edge Cases]

## Requirement Coverage

- [x] CHK020 Are structurally invalid, zero-solution, unique-solution, and multiple-solution cases separately covered by requirements and success criteria? [Coverage, Spec §US1, §Edge Cases, §SC-001–002]
- [x] CHK021 Are invalid, ambiguous, unclassifiable, and budget-exhausted generation candidates all explicitly rejected without changing the requested difficulty? [Coverage, Spec §US2, §FR-007, §FR-010, §SC-005]
- [x] CHK022 Are cancellation requests during both generation and difficulty analysis covered, including cancellation before publication? [Coverage, Spec §US2, §Edge Cases, §FR-008, §SC-004]
- [x] CHK023 Do the requirements make all four requested levels meaningful and classifiable, rather than allowing a documented profile with no supported solving techniques? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005–007, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK024 Is the offline/no-external-service constraint stated consistently for the full generation and uniqueness flow? [Coverage, Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add review findings inline and link them to the relevant spec or plan section.
- Items are numbered sequentially for this newly created checklist.
